themes.title: General-purpose humanoids
themes.description: Tesla is still routing every Optimus unit to its own factories and internal "Optimus Academy," not customers, with first enterprise sales targeted late 2026 and consumer availability pushed to end of 2027. The real near-term test is a promised public reveal of Optimus performing genuine, unscripted factory work, expected late September/October — the milestone that would finally settle the autonomous-vs-teleoperated debate. Figure AI's Nscale compute deal (up to 100,000 NVIDIA Vera Rubin GPUs, $3.5B initial commitment) stands from last week. Unitree launched its upgraded G1+ (six major updates) on Sep 15, but the product news hasn't moved its still-battered stock.

themes.title: Warehouse & logistics automation
themes.description: Symbotic shares have stabilized in the low-$40s (~$41.93, Sep 19) but the sell-side keeps cutting: Needham lowered its target to $60 from $75 on Sep 15, the second reduction in two weeks after Barclays' Sep 8 cut to $38. Consensus is now Hold, with an average target of $62.09 across 11 analysts — sentiment still lagging the underlying GAAP-profitable, $721M-revenue business.

themes.title: Surgical robotics
themes.description: Intuitive Surgical jumped to $383.54 (Sep 17, from $353.24) on EU approval of da Vinci SP for gynecologic surgery, though shares remain down ~34% YTD — on pace for the weakest year since 2008 — against a $508.68 average target. The competitive backdrop got sharper this week too: J&J's Ottava, FDA de novo-authorized in July for 10 general surgery procedures, got a high-profile CNBC feature (Sep 11) framing its table-integrated four-arm design — 30-50% smaller footprint than cart-based systems — as a genuine challenge to da Vinci's two-decade soft-tissue monopoly. Medtronic's Hugo (FDA-cleared for urologic procedures) also unveiled a new AI compute platform built for the operating room the same week as Ottava's clearance.

themes.title: Defense autonomy & drones
themes.description: AeroVironment shares have climbed to roughly $160 by Sep 20 — up about 14% off the post-earnings low of $140.80 — as the market gradually catches up to the Sep 9 beat, record $1.5B backlog and expanding margins. Kratos is increasingly framed as a laser-weapons rival to AeroVironment, posting 30.5% YoY Q2 revenue growth on top of its own $2.08B backlog. The contracts-vs-stock-price disconnect that defined this sub-sector in early September is finally starting to close, at least for AVAV.

themes.title: Field robotics
themes.description: No major new developments this week beyond the already-known Caterpillar/FieldAI physical-AI partnership (formalized Sep 5) and Deere's ongoing autonomous-mower rollout. Both remain diversified industrials where robotics is a small slice of the overall investment case.

themes.title: Japanese factory automation
themes.description: Fanuc has bounced modestly to ¥5,852 (Sep 19) from ¥5,735 the prior week, but remains well off its ¥7,334 average target even with an intact 8-buy/1-sell consensus rating — a bounce, not yet a recovery. Keyence and Yaskawa saw no fresh company-specific news this week.

themes.title: Supply chain & components
themes.description: Vishay Precision Group is this week's standout: its analyst price target nearly doubled to $77 from $39 after a formal vendor nomination letter from an unnamed humanoid robotics developer — a concrete signal rather than narrative. Shares have actually pulled back about 11% over the past month to $60.49, widening the gap between price and the new target. Harmonic Drive is little changed near ¥5,790. Cognex raised its through-cycle adjusted EBITDA target to 25-31%, aiming for a 25% run-rate exiting 2026.

themes.title: The robot "brain"
themes.description: NVIDIA pushed the stack further this week with the open Isaac GR00T N1.6 vision-language-action model and the Newton Physics Engine now built into Isaac Lab, plus a new Blackwell-architecture Jetson T4000 module delivering roughly 4x the energy efficiency of its predecessor. Agility Robotics, Boston Dynamics, Disney Research, Figure AI, Franka Robotics, Hexagon and Skild AI are all building on the platform. NVDA shares trade near $219 (Sep 17, ~$5.3T market cap) against a $328.66 consensus target.

themes.title: China scaling & listing
themes.description: Unitree's market cap has roughly stabilized near $30.3B — still down ~54% from its Aug 19 peak — even after the Sep 15 G1+ launch. Chatham House now pegs that reduced cap at roughly 125x 2025 revenue, underscoring how far valuations still have to normalize. The FCC's foreign-humanoid import ban remains in force, and it's set to be tested directly: Xi Jinping's planned Sep 24 state visit to meet President Trump puts the policy in the spotlight, with Beijing having called it damaging to bilateral relations.

bear_case.title: Unitree's valuation still looks stretched even after halving
bear_case.description: Market cap has roughly stabilized near $30.3B — still down ~54% from the $66B intraday peak — even after the Sep 15 G1+ launch. Chatham House now pegs that reduced cap at roughly 125x 2025 revenue. One Korean-market estimate put the erosion at 48 trillion won (~$34B) in just three weeks. China's own National Development and Reform Commission has separately warned of a domestic robotics bubble, specifically flagging startups producing near-identical machines.

bear_case.title: The market is still pricing out Optimus's near-term case
bear_case.description: Polymarket odds of a commercial Tesla Optimus launch by end-2026 remain near ~9%, down from ~33% a month earlier. The promised public reveal of genuine, unscripted factory work — expected late September/October — is the real test; until it lands, the timeline skepticism priced into the prediction market stands.

bear_case.title: Humanoid funding still outruns humanoid revenue
bear_case.description: Roughly $56B has flowed into robotics companies in 2026 — nearly double the prior year's full-year record. Figure AI's $39B valuation looks particularly exposed: third-party estimates put its 2025 shipments at only around 150 robots, implying annual revenue in the low tens of millions at best. Most of the venture-funded humanoid field still doesn't have revenue that comes close to justifying its price tag.

bear_case.title: Demos ≠ autonomy
bear_case.description: If a humanoid demo isn't explicitly labeled autonomous, assume teleoperation. Tesla's own pending "unscripted factory work" reveal is precisely the test of this distinction — dexterity, inference speed, reliability and cost still confine most real deployments to structured factory/warehouse tasks.

bear_case.title: Crowding & shakeout risk
bear_case.description: 150+ companies chasing humanoids, with Agibot alone claiming 15,000 cumulative units shipped; a reshuffling of startups is widely expected. Robotics pioneer Rodney Brooks argues much of the investment will be wasted.

bear_case.title: Sentiment can eventually catch up to fundamentals — in both directions
bear_case.description: AeroVironment's stock has climbed ~14% off its post-earnings low over the past two weeks as the market finally credits the Sep 9 beat and record backlog. Symbotic shows the opposite pattern: still GAAP-profitable with $721M in quarterly revenue, yet Needham cut its target again on Sep 15 — the second cut in two weeks. The same disconnect between fundamentals and price can resolve either way, and investors shouldn't assume which direction it breaks for any given name.

bear_case.title: Revenue is elsewhere
bear_case.description: Industrial, logistics, and surgical robots generate proven revenue today; humanoids largely don't yet. The surgical sub-sector is a useful reminder: da Vinci, Ottava and Hugo are all fighting over real procedure volume and real dollars, not speculative future demand.

bear_case.title: China price war
bear_case.description: 150+ Chinese humanoid startups, now including BYD, are competing on price and scale even as Unitree's own stock struggles to hold its valuation and Beijing's planners flag the same crowding risk. Xi Jinping's planned Sep 24 US visit is a catalyst to watch for any softening — or escalation — of the FCC's import ban given China's roughly 85% share of global humanoid shipments.

bear_case.title: "Late-stage bubble" warnings keep stacking up
bear_case.description: A September 14 Fortune piece described "crazy days" and "silly season" in markets amid talk of a late-stage AI bubble finally popping, with robotics and space repeatedly flagged as key risk areas. KB Securities has likened 2026's robotics/space enthusiasm to the final stage of the dot-com bubble; Ray Dalio has separately compared the broader AI bubble to 1929 and 2000 valuation extremes.

positions.name: Harmonic Drive
positions.note: Shares little changed near ¥5,790 against a ¥7,731 average target (7-buy/1-sell) — still needs the humanoid actuator order book to convert more consistently before adding back.

positions.name: Intuitive Surgical
positions.note: EU approval for da Vinci SP in gynecologic surgery pushed shares up to $383.54, but J&J's Ottava got a high-profile CNBC feature this week (Sep 11) calling it a genuine challenge to da Vinci's two-decade soft-tissue monopoly. Still down ~34% YTD; the competitive question just got more concrete, so still Watch rather than Core.

positions.name: Cognex
positions.note: Raised its through-cycle adjusted EBITDA target to 25-31%, aiming for a 25% run-rate exiting 2026 — a real positive — but still digesting the earlier HSBC downgrade to Hold; one good guidance update isn't yet enough to move off the sidelines.

positions.name: Caterpillar
positions.note: No new catalyst this specific week beyond the already-known FieldAI partnership; robotics remains a rounding error next to the construction-cycle exposure you'd actually be buying.

positions.name: Fanuc
positions.note: Shares have bounced modestly to ¥5,852 (Sep 19) from ¥5,735, but remain well off the ¥7,334 average target despite an intact 8-buy/1-sell rating — a bounce, not a recovery.

positions.name: ABB Ltd
positions.note: Still awaiting regulatory clearance on the SoftBank robotics sale with no new update this week; little left here to hold for ahead of a mid-to-late-2026 close.

positions.name: Serve Robotics
positions.note: No fresh catalyst this week after last month's guidance cut to $9-10M for FY26; revenue growth still isn't outrunning the downward guidance revisions.

positions.name: Johnson & Johnson
positions.note: Ottava's FDA de novo authorization (10 general surgery procedures, granted Jul 22) got a fresh CNBC profile this week (Sep 11) describing a table-integrated design that takes 30-50% less space than cart-based systems like da Vinci — a real competitive signal for surgical robotics. But robotics is a rounding error inside a $450B+ diversified healthcare conglomerate; added to track the Ottava-vs-da Vinci dynamic, not for JNJ's own exposure.

positions.name: Tesla
positions.note: No commercial Optimus units shipped; Polymarket's ~9% odds of a launch by end-2026 are unchanged. The next real test is the promised public reveal of unscripted factory work, expected late September/October — until that lands, still Avoid.

positions.name: Unitree
positions.note: Market cap has roughly stabilized near $30.3B (down ~54% from the $66B peak) even after the Sep 15 G1+ launch — a product update hasn't moved the stock. Chatham House pegs the current cap at ~125x 2025 revenue; the FCC ban and China's own NDRC bubble warning both remain firmly in place.
